title: Bacon Sandwich
subtitle: Crisp back bacon in soft white bread with ketchup or brown sauce
excerpt: Crisp back bacon in soft white bread with ketchup or HP sauce. One of the most consistently described meals in British life, made at home and in every cafe in the country.
sourceNotes: The bacon sandwich in white bread is a documented British working breakfast from at least the late Victorian period, found in factory canteen records and cookery columns from the early twentieth century. Nigel Slater, Toast: The Story of a Boy's Hunger (2003), informal reference. Recipe developed from first principles.

content.text: A bacon sandwich is three or four rashers of back bacon fried until crisp at the edges, put into soft white bread with ketchup or brown sauce. The bread matters: thick-cut white sandwich bread is the standard. The bacon needs high heat so the fat renders and the edges catch. Do not use a lid: it steams the bacon rather than frying it.
Heat a frying pan over high heat for 2 minutes. No oil needed: the bacon fat is enough.

Lay {{back-bacon}} rashers in the pan. Fry without moving for 2 to 3 minutes until the undersides are browned and slightly crisp. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more. The fat at the edges should be golden and just catching.
While the bacon cooks, butter {{bread-white}} slices if using. Lay the hot bacon onto two slices. Add ketchup or brown sauce. Close with the second slice, press lightly, and cut in half.

rows.cause: Pan not hot enough or too many rashers in the pan at once
rows.fix: Fry in a very hot pan with no more than 4 rashers at a time. The pan must be properly hot before the bacon goes in.

rows.cause: Pan not hot enough or moved too soon
rows.fix: Wait until the bacon releases naturally before turning. A hot pan prevents sticking better than oil does.

rows.cause: Bacon put on too fast while still wet with fat, or wet tomato sauce added first
rows.fix: Lift the bacon from the pan and drain briefly on a piece of kitchen paper. Put the sauce on the bread before the bacon, not after.

rows.cause: Heat too low or cooking time too short
rows.fix: High heat is essential. The fat on the edge should sizzle actively and colour to gold.

content.text: The bacon sandwich is as close as British food comes to a universal. It appears at breakfast, mid-morning, and after a late night. The ketchup versus brown sauce debate is one of the few tribal food arguments in the country. Back bacon, the British cut with a round of lean meat and a tail of streaky, is different from American-style streaky bacon and gives the sandwich its particular combination of crisp edge and tender lean centre.
